warehouse.orm-entity.ts: WarehouseOrmEntity is declared with @Entity('warehouse', { schema: 'warehouse' }). Its @OneToMany(() => OrderOrmEntity, (order) => order.warehouse, { cascade: ['insert','update'] }) is the inverse side. Cascade is set only on this side, so it is not duplicated.

The incoming users (warehouse.mapper.ts, warehouse.repository.ts, and the modules) all consume the pair as a single persistence model.

They use the same abstraction, TypeORM decorators. The Order↔Warehouse relationship is declared once from each side, as TypeORM requires. The two sides agree on the inverse properties, and only the owning side defines the join column. No business rule or invariant is repeated, and neither file goes around a module abstraction. The two files import each other, but they reference each other through lazy arrow functions, which is the standard TypeORM pattern. That makes it expected coupling within one unit, not a split.
